_comment: Captured on 2026-11-20 with the engine as it was before D-093 (the simplification branch at a468819): made-up clients and locations with voice and policy layers at every level, as the engine stored them in voice_profiles and reply_policies, and for each location what domain::resolve_settings gave and the fingerprint of that. Giving every location one complete row must change none of them. Never regenerate this file.

topics.label: Freshness and restocking (empty trays, slow refills)
Concept or name expectations (e.g. cuisine not what the name suggests)

item_types.description: A named dish or food item (e.g. sushi, crab legs, hot and sour soup, pho).
A drink (e.g. bubble tea, soda, beer).
A buffet station or section (e.g. sushi bar, hibachi grill, dim sum, noodle soup station, seafood).
A staff member named in the review: a server, host, chef or manager (first name only, as the reviewer wrote it).

severity_flags.label: Illness or food poisoning
severity_flags.description: The reviewer or someone in their party got sick (stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, hospital visit) after eating here, or says they suspect food poisoning. Raise it even when the rating is high or the reviewer is unsure of the cause.

severity_flags.label: Allergen incident
severity_flags.description: An allergic reaction, or an allergen (nuts, shellfish, gluten, dairy, egg, soy, sesame and so on) that was served despite a warning or was not labelled. Includes "almost" incidents where the reviewer caught it in time.

severity_flags.label: Foreign object in food
severity_flags.description: Hair, glass, plastic, metal, a bandage, an insect, a pest or any other object that should not be in the food or drink, or pests seen in the restaurant.

severity_flags.label: Food safety and handling
severity_flags.description: Spoiled, expired or rotten food; raw or undercooked meat or seafood; cold food that should be hot, or sushi and seafood left warm; visibly unsafe food handling.

severity_flags.label: Hygiene
severity_flags.description: Unsanitary conditions that could affect health: dirty, greasy or wet plates, bowls, cups or utensils; food residue on tableware; staff handling food with unwashed hands; filthy restrooms. General "could be cleaner" remarks go under the cleanliness topic instead.

severity_flags.label: Discrimination or harassment
severity_flags.description: The reviewer says they, or someone with them, were treated differently or badly because of race, ethnicity, language, religion, gender, sexuality, age, disability or similar; or were harassed, followed, profiled or humiliated by staff.

severity_flags.label: Staff misconduct
severity_flags.description: Staff behaved in a seriously improper way beyond poor service: theft, intoxication at work, physical aggression, verbal abuse, threats, recording customers, fraud or overcharging on purpose, or tampering with food or belongings.

severity_flags.label: Legal or regulatory threat
severity_flags.description: The reviewer threatens or reports legal action, a lawyer, a lawsuit, police, or a complaint to a health department, licensing board, consumer protection agency or similar regulator.

severity_flags.label: Threat of violence
severity_flags.description: The reviewer threatens to harm staff, the owner, customers or the property, or describes an intention to commit violence (including arson or vandalism).

topics.label: Relaxation and results (scalp, skin, pain relief)
Booking, scheduling, timing and treatment length
Communication, language and listening to requests
Hair drying and styling after treatment

item_types.description: A named treatment or package (e.g. head spa, scalp treatment, gua sha facial, foot massage, deep tissue massage, combo).
A staff member named in the review (first name only, as the reviewer wrote it).
A product used or sold (oil, shampoo, mask).
An amenity (tea and snacks, steam, water ring, blow-dry, room with fountain).

severity_flags.label: Injury
severity_flags.description: Physical harm during or after a treatment: lasting pain ("still in pain"), bruising, burns, cuts, strains, hair or scalp damage, being hit, or a treatment so rough it hurt. Ordinary "strong pressure" that the reviewer liked is NOT an injury.

severity_flags.label: Allergic or skin reaction
severity_flags.description: Rash, redness, hives, swelling, breakouts, burning or itching skin or scalp, or eye irritation after a facial, scalp treatment, oil or product.

severity_flags.label: Hygiene
severity_flags.description: Unsanitary conditions that could affect health: dirty or reused towels, sheets or tools, hair or stains on linens, unwashed hands, bugs, mold, dirty water. General "could be cleaner" remarks go under the cleanliness topic instead.

severity_flags.label: Inappropriate conduct by staff
severity_flags.description: Sexual or inappropriate touching, assault, comments of a sexual nature, draping violations, a therapist making the guest feel unsafe, or any allegation of assault. Always raise it on an allegation, even if vague.

severity_flags.description: Staff behaved in a seriously improper way beyond poor service: theft, intoxication at work, physical aggression, verbal abuse, threats, recording customers, fraud or overcharging on purpose, or tampering with food or belongings.

severity_flags.description: The reviewer threatens or reports legal action, a lawyer, a lawsuit, police, or a complaint to a health department, licensing board, consumer protection agency or similar regulator.

business_facts: An all-you-can-eat buffet in a suburban shopping plaza, which opened recently in a renovated space that used to be a different buffet.
The buffet is mostly Chinese and pan-Asian food with sushi, seafood, dim sum, a noodle soup station and desserts.
Lunch and dinner are priced differently, with seniors and children priced separately.
style_notes: Five-star replies are two or three sentences. Thank the guest, name a dish or station they liked, invite them back.
Never argue with the reviewer.
Do not defend the food with claims you cannot check (e.g. "our ingredients are freshly purchased").
For complaints, apologise for the specific issue (restocking, temperature, cleanliness, seasoning) and say the team will review it; do not promise a specific fix or date.
Do not address the reviewer by name; we never know it.
example_replies: Thank you for the kind review. We're glad the sushi and the seafood were to your liking, and we look forward to your next visit.
Thank you for your honest feedback. We apologize that the dim sum station sat empty during your visit. We will review this with our team.
voice.base_style: Polished hospitality. Gracious and composed, like a good hotel front desk. Complete sentences, no slang, no emoji.

business_facts: A head spa and wellness studio in New York City with two locations.
Treatments include head spa and scalp care, massage, foot massage, gua sha sculpting facials and combination packages.
A rough blow-dry follows the head spa; it is not a professional salon blowout.
style_notes: Five-star replies are one to three short sentences. Thank the guest, echo one detail (treatment, therapist, space), invite them back.
If the reviewer names a therapist, mention that therapist by name ("We'll share your kind words with Eva!").
Do not address the reviewer by name; we never know it.
A Chinese reply is warm and natural (e.g. 谢谢您的好评！很开心您喜欢这次头疗，期待下次再见～). Light emoji is fine.
For complaints, apologise sincerely, show you understood the specific issue, and invite the guest to contact the spa directly by "reaching out to us" without giving a phone, email or link.
example_replies: Thank you for the lovely review! So happy the head spa left you relaxed. See you again soon 🤍
We'll pass your kind words on to Eva! Thank you for coming in ✨
谢谢您的好评！💕 很高兴您喜欢我们的环境，期待下次再为您服务！
voice.base_style: Warm and casual. Friendly and upbeat, like a host who remembers you. Short sentences, light exclamation marks, a little emoji.

style_notes: Keep it to two sentences.
voice.base_style: Warm and casual. Short, friendly sentences.
